claim: Stem calls Watford a 'Premier League club'. q: Which Premier League club is nicknamed 'The Hornets' and plays in yellow and black?

claim: 'ending their dream run in the group stage' misdescribes what happened. South Africa had no 'dream run' — they drew their opener with Mexico, then lost 3-0 to Uruguay in match two, and were still alive going into the final group game, which they won 2-1 against France; they went out on goal difference after that match, not because of the Uruguay defeat. So Uruguay's win neither ended a run nor eliminated them. The answer (Uruguay were the only side to beat the hosts) is unaffected.
q: Which country beat hosts South Africa at the 2010 World Cup — ending their dream run in the group stage?

claim: Stem asserts Steaua Bucharest's 104 games is "the record for the longest unbeaten run in domestic top-flight football". It is not the world record — ASEC Mimosas of Ivory Coast went 108 consecutive league games unbeaten (1989–1994, ended by a defeat to SO de l'Armée). Steaua's 104 (June 1986 – Sept 1989) is the EUROPEAN record. The keyed option is fine; the superlative in the stem is false and teaches a wrong fact. Fix: qualify as "in European domestic football".
q: Which club holds the record for the longest unbeaten run in domestic top-flight football, with 104 consecutive league games?
